meta.title: KP Front – Digital incident command for fire brigades
meta.description: KP Front is the digital command post at the scene: map, plans, teams, log and report – offline-capable and open source.
meta.ogTitle: KP Front – Digital incident command for fire brigades
meta.ogDescription: The digital command post at the scene: map, plans, teams, log and report – offline-capable and open source.

schema.description: Digital incident command and situation map for fire brigades – with swisstopo maps, tactical symbols to FKS conventions, SCBA monitoring and a running incident log.
featureList: Situation map on swisstopo maps with tactical symbols to FKS conventions
SCBA monitoring with pressure, turnaround time, contact clock and alarms
Building and object plans as a whiteboard for drawing and measuring
Incident log that is only added to and never rewritten
Shift planning for long incidents, with a coverage view
Incident report as a PDF, pre-filled from the incident data
Replay: play the incident back for the debrief

hero.h1: Digital incident command for the fire brigade.
hero.lede: KP Front is the digital command post at the scene: map, plans, teams, log and report in one app.
hero.ctaNote: No login – in the demo, Musterdorf is on fire right now (interface in German)
hero.frameAlt: Map view: tactical symbols to Swiss FKS conventions, sectors and hose lines

fit.note: Grown out of the real operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – proven there, and developed further with every incident.

own.p: KP Front is open source and runs on a machine in your own station or in your own cloud. Incident data, plans, crews and reports stay under your control.
items: No licence fees
No vendor lock-in
Run it yourself and adapt it to your needs

tenet.quote: «Usable at 3am – after six months without practice»
tenet.expl: In a militia fire brigade nobody sits at the screen every day. So the app has to be built for someone half asleep to get right: everything that matters visible at once, sensible defaults instead of settings, and every action can be undone.

incident.eyebrow: From the call to the report
incident.lede:
This is what a night with KP Front looks like – the map, the teams and the
        documentation stay consistent and traceable for everyone involved.

entries.p:
Take over an alert from your paging system (e. g. Divera or FireHub) with one tap – or start
            by hand from an address, a building or the map. The location and the building data are
            there before the first appliance rolls.

entries.h3: The first situation picture is up.
entries.p:
FKS tactical symbols, sectors, hose lines and notes on the digital situation map.
            Hydrants, utility lines and vehicle positions sit underneath as layers.

Cylinder pressure, turnaround time and contact clock run per team. The app speaks up
            before it gets tight – even when nobody happens to be watching the clock.

entries.h3: The building plan becomes a whiteboard.
entries.p:
Open the pre-incident plan, draw on it, place teams, measure to scale –
            with the same tools as on the map.

Type it, or simply speak it – when a transcription service is configured, voice
            memos can be turned into text; otherwise they stay as audio in the log. The log is
            only ever added to, never rewritten – corrections use new entries, not an eraser.

If it turns into a long night, the shift plan holds, per person, from when to when
            they are available and when they are rostered. The coverage line shows where there
            are too few people – before the gap is there. Attendance is untouched by it:
            planning happens here, ticking off happens there.

entries.h3: By the time you head back, the report is nearly done.
entries.p:
Situation, crew, material and log flow straight into the incident report.
            Nobody has to reconstruct the night from memory afterwards.

For the debrief, the replay plays the whole incident back: situation, teams and log
            exactly as they stood at any given minute. It skips the long waits – four hours
            become a few minutes.

None of this is broken today – the paper situation map has worked for decades.
        KP Front steps into the same places, only without the copying out.

A plan you can draw on

features.lede: Grown at real incidents and exercises, not from a feature list. Everything that comes from outside – paging, GPS, Microsoft sign-in – is optional: KP Front runs perfectly well without any of those connections.

items: Tactical symbols to FKS conventions, with attributes and labelling
Sectors, cordons, areas and freehand drawing
Hose lines with FKS annotations, each assigned to a team
Measuring distance and area, to scale on the plan as well
Layers: hydrants, utility cadastre, cantonal map services
Hazardous materials reference: UN numbers, substance information and guidance on isolation and protective distances, available directly during the incident
Weather and wind information to support the situation assessment, plus the MeteoSwiss precipitation radar as a layer
Building plans as a whiteboard and a stack of floors
Board with FKS pages: free sketch, First command and handbook sheets – printed in the report like the original
Building info: facts from the building register – gas, heating oil, solar PV – and the immediate measures for the object

Georeferencing: link a plan to the map through shared landmarks – one object, visible on both surfaces, with an honest read-out of the accuracy. The station has its plans aligned ahead of time and approves them
Undo/redo on every surface – documented events remain traceable
SCBA monitoring: pressure, turnaround time, contact clock, alarms
SCBA emergency: a team in trouble turns red at the top of every device at once – with an emergency clock and the safety team
Teams with or without breathing apparatus: crew, assignment and team leader – on the map, on the plan and in the stack of floors, each with its own team colour, the same everywhere
Attendance with arrival times and ranks
On the way: who has confirmed the Divera alert, right above attendance
Shift plan: plan availability and shifts per person, see coverage across the incident and print command forms
Share location: whoever opens the link appears as a dot on the situation map – voluntary, and only for this incident
Share the incident by link; access is clearly indicated and can be revoked at any time
Material with stock and consumption
Checklists for command support and incident command
Incident commander role: keep attendance, resources, checklists and the report – read the map and the teams without moving anything
A log that is only added to and never rewritten
Voice memos with transcription, photos, reminders
Replay: play the incident back minute by minute, waits skipped – for the debrief

Ready-made incident report as a PDF, including crew, material, times, log, sketch,
            photos and SCBA monitoring
Debrief sheet for the after-action review: key figures and a timeline on a page of its own at the end of the report
Photos as attachments to the report
Completion check: before closing, KP Front shows which information or clarifications are still missing from the report
Partner organisations with their remarks in the report
A capture sheet by QR code for everyone who has something to contribute
Alert and incident times from what actually happened, not from memory
Offline-capable as an installable app – the readiness check shows before an incident whether the required data is on the device
Several connected devices work on the same state – after a connection interruption, changes are synchronised again
Roles: edit, or read along only
Day/night mode, symbol size, large touch targets for the tablet
Can take over alerts from Divera or FireHub; further alerting systems can be connected through the open interface optional
Vehicle positions by GPS optional
Sign in with Microsoft to an existing account, alongside the PIN optional
Object visits without an incident, offline – checklist, photos and report optional
Your own administration area per fire brigade: crew, vehicles, checklists, map layers and templates

sibling.h2: KP Front commands at the front. KP Rück keeps the overview behind it.
sibling.p: KP Rück is the digital version of the magnetic board in the rear command post: one board for personnel, vehicles and equipment. Its own app, the same handwriting – both take the same alarm from the dispatch system, and neither needs the other.
sibling.cta: Take a look at KP Rück

setup.h3: Running both – without setting everything up twice

rows.dd: The same payload for both. Your dispatch integration is built once; each app only gets its own address.
One key for both – the same alarms, the same roster. optional
The same source in the same file format – the same person on both sides.
The same alarm keyword list, so the same classification in both apps.

setup.foot: Database, updates and login stay separate. Neither one needs the other to run.

items.a:
Everyone sees the same situation at the same time – in the command vehicle, on the
          tablet and with the incident commander. No message is lost on a scrap of paper. The SCBA
          monitoring speaks up by itself before it gets tight. Less radio traffic for questions
          that are already answered on the situation picture – and the report is nearly done as
          you head back, instead of the weekend after. KP Front helps the incident commander keep
          the situation free of contradictions and make the odd one out visible: a team out of
          radio contact, an appliance that is nowhere, a check-in that never came.

items.q: Where is sensitive incident data stored?
items.a: Every fire brigade runs KP Front itself (self-hosted). Incident data – situation map, SCBA monitoring, log and building plans – stays on its own installation and its own devices: for example a mini-PC at the station, its own server or a cloud provider it chooses. There is no central server, and nothing is sent automatically to a vendor or to us. Map, address and weather services (swisstopo among them by default) receive only the location being requested; other external services run only when the brigade sets them up itself.

items.q: How does KP Front differ from commercial systems?
items.a: KP Front is open source (AGPL-3.0): no licence fees, no subscription, no per-device fee. Every fire brigade runs its own installation and so keeps control of its data. What remains are its own costs for operation, infrastructure and any external support. Development comes straight from the practice of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL; bug reports, ideas and contributions from the open-source community are welcome.

items.q: What does it take to run?
items.a:
A small mini-PC or server at the station is enough. Setup, updates and backups
          require someone with Docker and command-line experience, whether in the brigade, the
          municipality or an IT support provider. The guide and administration area lead through
          the setup. We are happy to answer general questions; data and operation remain the
          responsibility of each fire brigade.

items.q: Is support available for installation and operation?
items.a: Yes. General questions about installation and use can be answered free of charge. KP Front can be operated on an organisation’s own infrastructure or with a hosting or cloud provider of its choice. Support with installation, configuration, updates or operation is also available by individual agreement. More extensive support may be subject to a fee.

items.q: Does KP Front work without an internet connection?
items.a: Yes. As an installed app, KP Front runs on the device: map, plans, teams and log stay usable even when the network drops. The app loads the maps and plans around an incident by itself, shortly after it is opened – and the readiness check shows before an incident whether the required data is on the device. After an interruption, changes are synchronised again as soon as a connection is available; whatever was recorded in the meantime is kept.

items.q: Can we adapt it to how we work?
items.a: Yes. Every fire brigade has its own administration area: crew, vehicles, doctrine and templates are all set there. Checklists, building plans and map layers come from your own station data and are loaded with the command-line tools that ship with it. And because the whole code is on GitHub , anything else can be built – by you or to your order.

items.q: Does KP Front only work in Switzerland?
items.a: No. As open-source software, KP Front is freely available and can be adapted to local conditions anywhere in the world. Out of the box it is preconfigured for Switzerland – with swisstopo maps, tactical symbols to FKS conventions and the FKS templates for incident command. Outside Switzerland other base maps can be configured; address search currently supports only the swisstopo interface and needs adapting there.

items.q: Which languages are available for KP Front?
items.a: The KP Front user interface is currently available in German. As an open-source application, KP Front can be extended to further languages. This requires a complete translation of the firefighting terminology and a professional review.

With the demo, no sign-up – Musterdorf is already on fire, and all visitors share the same incident (it restarts at midnight and at noon). Then try it at an exercise. If it fits, the setup guide leads to your own installation.

contact.p:
Do you want to try KP Front at your fire brigade? Is something missing, or does
          something not work the way you expect? Get in touch – we read everything.
contact.alt: For questions and open-ended ideas there are the GitHub discussions.

footer.origin: Born out of the operational work of Feuerwehr Oberwil BL – because at incident after incident we kept seeing the same sources of error: double bookings, information scattered across places, and transcription mistakes made by hand. Every fire brigade runs its own KP Front, with its own maps, plans and data.
